## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `--exclude` flag needs to read its default from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE`, because the project's CLI flag rules require this for every new flag under `cli/`. The flag's matching behaviour is covered by added tests that assert outcomes: the archive contents and the collected paths.

## Changes
The pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` flag that makes `collect` skip any file whose basename matches one of the patterns, and logs each skipped file. It also documents the flag in `docs/flags.md` and adds parser, `collect` and end-to-end tests, plus a text fixture.

(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Read the --exclude default from ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE — Setting `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE=*.log` in CI has no effect, because the flag hard-codes `default=[]`. `.claude/skills/cli-flags/reference.md:5` says: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable". — CI jobs that set options through the environment cannot exclude files, which breaks the project's CLI contract for new flags. — Fix: Build the default from `os.environ.get("ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE")`, choose and document how multiple patterns are separated, and add a test next to `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing`.
